const.syntax: literal dot ASCII-class negated-ASCII-class concatenation optional star plus initial-caret terminal-dollar
const.classes: ASCII units and inclusive non-reversed ASCII ranges; escape bracket dash and backslash; non-ASCII class entries rejected; negated class includes unmatched non-ASCII scalars
const.unsupported: groups alternation bounded-repeat lazy-quantifiers lookaround backreference named-character-class Unicode-property
const.text: strict valid UTF-8; case-sensitive; no normalization; NUL and CR are literal data
const.empty: Some offset 0 length 0; distinct from None

const.scratch: 2 * (actual atom count + 1) UIntSize cells; zero means inactive, byte-start-plus-one means earliest live start
const.step: one cell initialize/clear, input iteration, atom parse, or class-entry parse/match; Unicode scalar comparison/advance is at most four bytes
const.constructor: linear pattern-byte bound; initial parser fuel=maxPatternBytes, one atom plus one class entry never exceeds consumed pattern bytes
const.find: O((input scalars + 1) * (pattern bytes + atoms + 1)); no recursion or backtracking
const.precedence: InvalidLimits -> PatternLimit -> left-to-right syntax then AtomLimit per atom; find InputLimit -> ScratchTooSmall -> WorkLimit

const.pattern: borrows source owner through SourceText; immutable and private state
const.input: borrowed only during find; Match retains neither input nor scratch
const.scratch: caller-owned two banks; no allocation/resizing; visible length/capacity and suffix preserved
const.errors: InputLimit and ScratchTooSmall preserve all scratch bytes; WorkLimit may mutate prefix, retry initializes prefix anew; no partial Match on exhaustion
const.positions: UTF-8 byte offsets; requiredCells nonzero only on ScratchTooSmall

const.reference: Go regexp.Compile then Longest then FindStringIndex on valid UTF-8 only
const.allocation: transitive whole-module direct-call closure; no allocator or unresolved callee permitted
const.native: managed Windows exact and official golden; Linux exact separately
